items.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21
items.q: The interviewee refers to Buddy as 'Papa Trombone' and discusses his reputation ('one of the best trombone jails in New Orleans ever'), but does not describe a direct personal interaction, collaboration, or mentorship with him.

ctx.x: Chook? Chook. Chook. That's what his name is, Chook. I don't know what his name is.
Chook. Chook. You take Lundy. You take Harrison Lundy, Bill Lundy, Boogerman Lundy, Yank didn't Lundy because Buddy wouldn't name him at home. He'd learn from Chook home, Yank. Oh yeah.
He did, yeah, because he used to follow us every Saturday night. Chook. I was playing in Gretna.

items.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21
items.q: the trombone that Booger Man had, that was my trombone... I give it to Booger.

ctx.x: Yeah. Somebody told me they thought you played trombone or something. I had a trombone.

But you never did play. No, the trombone that Booger Man had, that was my trombone. Well, that had been your trombone. That was mine. But you never did learn it. No. I'm crazy but bold. Yeah. And bold time come. I just... Yeah. See my old, my parrain, he was trying to blow a clarinet there. Who there was Robert Williams? Remember Robert Williams? Yeah, that's the guy. Oh yeah, you know, that's E.J. and William in Port Bratel. He had a clarinet. I had the trombone, you know, and when bold time come, I ain't study…
If you stayed up there, and I'd come back in high school, well, let's book ahead and try them all.
